take_homes: Having access to everything is not the same as using it. Count how much of the shared material actually gets cited before I promise anyone a rollout percentage.
Agents reading other agents' output invent sources unless the cite-the-file rule is built in. Same for an agent's summary of its own work, so push back on it.
A shared folder with one central synthesizer and a steering file can run a whole room of agents. The first wall to name is data access, runtime platform or discoverability.

monday.move: Run a small version of the forum with 5-6 people from sales and ops on one real company question, with the cite rule on and a count of how many folders the synthesizer's output cites.
monday.who: me, plus a few non-engineers who actually asked for it
monday.stop_condition: If the output cites fewer than a third of the folders, or nobody outside engineering opens the result, I stop and don't build the org-wide setup.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for this and I haven't decided who maintains the shared folder.

misconception.why: The line that nothing in the room checked the kernel hit the habit of skipping review that I'd just shown. I still think the individual checking steps in the exercises were ceremony, but I now accept that agent output and agent self-summaries need an outside check.

one_line: The first half is stuff I already do, but the shared-folder forum and the count of how much the room actually used from each other's work are worth the day. I'd send a leader who's never run a multi-agent setup.
